description: Frontend defense-in-depth cache-busting for the PDF Export links. Even with distinct keys from FEAT-002, the 'Already Generated' list and the freshly-generated link in mgmt/frontend/src/views/PdfExport.jsx render whatever URL the backend returns; appending a cache-buster derived from the record's generated_at (or the current timestamp for a just-generated file) guarantees the browser tab that opens the report cannot reuse a previously cached response for that exact URL. This is independent of FEAT-002 and cheap, but it does NOT replace it (it only affects in-app links, not the underlying object). Keep it minimal and consistent with the existing anchor rendering.
steps: In mgmt/frontend/src/views/PdfExport.jsx, add a tiny helper that appends a cache-buster query param to a URL (e.g. withCacheBuster(url, token) -> url + (url.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + 'v=' + encodeURIComponent(token)), guarding against null/empty urls.
Apply it to the freshly-generated download at a.href = res.publicLink (~L156-157): use a token like Date.now() or res.generated_at if present.

Apply it to the 'Already Generated' list anchors href={f.public_link} (~L229): use f.generated_at (fall back to f.id) as the token so the buster is stable per generation but changes when the file is regenerated.
Do not alter any other behavior of the component (labels, layout, warnings).

Add a vitest under mgmt/frontend/src/ (or the project's existing test location) asserting the rendered href for a previously-generated file carries the ?v=<token> buster, and that a URL already containing a query uses '&'. If there is no existing PdfExport test harness, add a focused component/unit test for the withCacheBuster helper and, if feasible with the existing setup, a render test for the anchor href. Follow whatever vitest/RTL pattern the frontend already uses; if none exists for views, a pure-function unit test of withCacheBuster is acceptable.
acceptance_criteria: The freshly-generated report link and every 'Already Generated' anchor href carry a ?v=<token> cache-buster.
withCacheBuster correctly uses '&' when the URL already has a query string and is a no-op for empty/null urls.
A vitest asserts the buster is present on the rendered href (or on withCacheBuster output).
cd mgmt/frontend && npx vitest run passes (no regressions).
verification: cd mgmt/frontend && npx vitest run  # green, new test passes
cd mgmt/frontend && npm run build  # builds clean
findings: Added exported pure helper withCacheBuster(url, token) to mgmt/frontend/src/views/PdfExport.jsx: no-op for empty/null url or missing (undefined/null/empty) token; appends '?v=' (or '&v=' when a query already exists) with encodeURIComponent(token). Applied to a.href for the freshly-generated download (token: res.generated_at || Date.now()) and to the 'Already Generated' anchor href (token: f.generated_at || f.id). No other behavior touched (labels, layout, warnings, generate flow unchanged). Test file src/views/PdfExport.test.jsx: mocks ../api.js (which has no heavy static deps), unit-tests the helper (plain-url ?v=, &v= when query present, token encoding incl. injection-safe '&'/'=', no-op on missing token, empty/null url safe, numeric token) AND a render test asserting the rendered anchor href carries ?v=<encoded generated_at>. node_modules already present so no npm ci needed. Verified: npx vitest run = 48 passed (4 files), 7 new; npm run build clean (PdfExport-*.js emitted). Frontend-only change; backend (1097) and render (203) suites untouched by this feature.
